title: Lithium-Ion Battery: Intercalation & Rocking-Chair Electrochemistry
pedagogical_goal: Visually demonstrate the microscopic and macroscopic working principles of a lithium-ion battery: how Li+ ions de-intercalate and migrate through the liquid electrolyte and porous separator between the graphite anode and cobalt oxide cathode, while electrons travel through the external circuit powering a load during discharge or being forced back by a power supply during charge.

components.description: Rounded cross-sectional battery cell showing three interior compartments: Negative Electrode (Anode, left x: 60-260), Porous Separator Zone (center x: 260-460), Positive Electrode (Cathode, right x: 460-660).
Horizontal stacked graphite layer planes where Li+ ions are intercalated between graphene sheets. Intercalation slots show glowing golden dots when occupied.
Vertical translucent porous membrane at center (x: 350-370) with micro-pore channels allowing Li+ ions to pass while visibly rejecting electrons.
Octahedral transition metal oxide crystal lattice layers (Cobalt Oxide) with interstitial sites accepting Li+ ions.
Golden glowing spheres (Li+) migrating across the electrolyte and through separator pores. Direction flips dynamically based on mode (Anode->Cathode during discharge; Cathode->Anode during charge).
Top electrical wire connecting negative copper terminal to positive aluminum terminal through a central device. Glowing blue electrons (e-) travel along the wire in sync with ion flow.
Central circuit device that switches between a glowing lightbulb (in Discharge mode, whose illumination scales with C-rate) and a DC power plug/lightning icon (in Charge mode).
Live battery state-of-charge percentage indicator with colored segment fill (Green > 60%, Amber 20-60%, Red < 20%).

lifecycle_rules: Use React useRef for container and SVG references
Manage all continuous ion and electron motion inside useEffect with gsap.context() and ctx.revert() cleanup
Drive continuous flow via gsap.ticker with timestep dt to update x/y coordinates of Li+ ions and circuit electrons
Smoothly tween battery fill gauges, voltage dials, and bulb brightness with gsap.to() on mode or slider changes
Reverse particle velocity vectors instantaneously when user toggles between 'Discharging' and 'Charging'

pedagogical_callouts.title: 1. The 'Rocking Chair' Principle
pedagogical_callouts.text: Unlike lead-acid or alkaline batteries where electrodes permanently dissolve or plate, a Li-ion battery is a 'rocking chair' system: lithium ions simply shuffle back and forth between the graphite anode layers and the cobalt oxide cathode lattice without losing their metallic ionic identity.

pedagogical_callouts.title: 2. The Separator & Electrolyte Barrier
pedagogical_callouts.text: The central porous membrane is an electronic insulator but an ionic conductor. It allows Li+ ions to diffuse through the liquid electrolyte, but strictly blocks electrons (e-), forcing them through the external wire to power your phone or motor!

pedagogical_callouts.title: 3. Discharge vs. Charge Cycles
pedagogical_callouts.text: During discharge, electrons flow spontaneously from negative to positive due to higher chemical potential at the anode. During charging, a higher external electrical voltage overcomes this gradient, forcibly pumping electrons and Li+ ions back into the graphite anode.
